To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the human PTH gene is regulated through cAMP-dependent pathway in HTLV-I infected T cells.
PTHRP gene transcription is enhanced through a PGE1-cAMP-dependent pathway in HTLV-I-transformed T cells.
the human PTHrp gene is activated through a cyclic AMP-dependent pathway by prostglandin E(1) in HTLV-I infected T cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the second messenger cAMP and its role in the regulation of parathyroid hormone (PTH)-related peptide (PTHrP) gene expression in HTLV-I infected T cells.
the role of the cAMP second messenger pathway in the regulation of parathyroid hormone related peptide (PTHrp) gene expression in human T-cell leukemia virus-I (HTLV-I)-infected T cells.
the regulation of the human Pthrp gene in HTLV-1 infected T cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PGE1 stimulates PTHRP gene transcription via the cAMP-dependent pathway in HTLV-I infected T-cell line MT-2, and that this stimulation is synergistic with interleukin-2.

prostaglandin-E1 stimulates the production of parathyroid-hormone-related peptide (PTHrP) in HTLV-I infected T cells by increasing the level of cAMP, which then increases the transcription of the PTHrP gene.
the PGE1-cAMP second messenger system plays an important role, but is not the only system in the regulation PTHRP gene transcription.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transcriptional regulation of the human PTHR gene in HTLV-1-infected T cells is mediated by the cAMP-dependent pathway.
PGE1 and PTHRP are involved in the development of ATL and hypercalcemia in these patients.
prostaglandins and interleukin 1 are involved in the regulation of PTHrP expression through a cAMP-mediated mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the human PTHrp gene is regulated by a cAMP-dependent transcriptional pathway in an HTLV-I-transformed T-cell line, and that prostaglandin-E1, as well its cAMP-dependent pathway, is a potent stimulator of the human Pthrp gene.

the human PTHrp gene is transcriptionally activated through the cAMP-dependent pathway and that the cAMP-dependent activation of PTHrp transcription is involved in the development of hyper-calcemia in ATL.
the transcription of human PTHrP gene is enhanced through cAMP-dependent pathway.
